samples.summary: Clicking an image never focuses the hidden textarea, so the new Cmd/Ctrl+C image-copy path can't fire when focus is elsewhere (notably read-only docs)
samples.evidence: The image hit branch of `handleImageMouseDown` (editor.ts:2502-2511) calls `e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation(); e.stopImmediatePropagation();` and sets `selectedImage`, but never calls `textEditor.focus()`. It is registered with `{capture: true}` (editor.ts:2522), so `TextEditor.handleMouseDown` — the only place that calls `this.focus()` (text-editor.ts:1673) — never runs for an image click. All the new plumbing (`imageKeyHandler`, `handleCopy`/`handleCut` image branches) is attached to the hidden textarea (text-editor.ts:560-565), so it only receives keydown/copy/cut when that textarea already has focus. In read-only mode the editor deliberately does NOT focus on mount (editor.ts:2757: `if (!readOnly) textEditor.focus();` with the comment that focus is 'acquired on first click … via handleMouseDown'), so a viewer whose first click is on an image gets no focus, no `copy` event, and issue #870 persists exactly as before. The same holds in edit mode whenever focus has moved to a toolbar/sidebar control before the image click.
searchedFor: grep focus() in text-editor.ts and editor.ts

samples.summary: The new cell-resolution path's stated invariant ("normalizeRange guarantees both endpoints share one cell") is false for tableCellRange selections, which can now reach sliceBlockRange with unordered / cross-cell endpoints
samples.evidence: `normalizeRange` only enforces same-cell ordering in the non-`tableCellRange` branch (selection.ts:132-172). The `tableCellRange` branch (selection.ts:120-128) returns `{start: range.anchor, end: range.focus}` verbatim — unordered and possibly in different cells. `handleCopy`/`handleCut` only skip `getSelectedBlocks()` when `getSelectedTableCells()` returns non-null, and that helper resolves the table via `layout.blocks.find(...)` (text-editor.ts:3711), which fails for a NESTED table, returning null. So a cell-rectangle copy inside a nested table now falls into the new `cellInfo` branch with unordered/cross-cell endpoints: `sliceBlockRange` may slice with `start.offset > end.offset` and emit a bogus one-empty-inline block on the clipboard where the old code returned `[]`.

samples.summary: The #872 fix does not cover the header/footer edit context: getSelectedBlocks still resolves against the body layout, so rich copy there still yields an empty payload
samples.evidence: `getSelectedBlocks()` calls `this.getLayout()` (body layout) rather than the edit-context layout used elsewhere (`this.editContext === 'header' ? this.getHeaderLayout() : ...`, text-editor.ts:4290, 4642). Header/footer block ids are not in `layout.blocks`, so `sliceBlockRange` returns `[]` and the clipboard keeps only text/plain — the same style/image loss #872 fixes for table cells. Header blocks nested in a header table are in the merged `blockParentMap` (editor.ts:1337-1338) but `resolveNestedTableLayout(..., layout)` is given the body layout, so that branch returns `[]` too.

samples.summary: handleCopy/handleCut preventDefault before knowing clipboardData is writable; if it is null the copy silently writes nothing while suppressing the native copy
samples.evidence: `e.preventDefault(); this.writeImageToClipboard(e, selected.image);` — `writeImageToClipboard` guards with `e.clipboardData?.setData(...)` (line 1269-1271), so a null `clipboardData` produces no write at all, yet the default action has already been suppressed. This is precisely the failure mode the provider's `findBlock` guard was added to avoid (editor.ts:2258-2261), just reached through a different door. In the cut path the image is additionally deleted from the document after nothing was written to the clipboard (line 1229-1230) — content loss with no clipboard copy.

samples.summary: navigator.platform-based mod-key detection silently misroutes Cmd+C on platforms that report an empty platform string, reintroducing #870
samples.evidence: `const mod = /Mac|iPhone|iPad|iPod/.test(navigator.platform) ? e.metaKey : e.ctrlKey;` — `navigator.platform` is deprecated and can be empty/frozen; when it does not match on a Mac, `mod` becomes `e.ctrlKey`, Cmd+C fails the new branch and falls through to the catch-all at line 2342 which clears `selectedImage`, so the subsequent `copy` event finds nothing. (Consistent with the existing idiom at text-editor.ts:874, so it is a shared weakness rather than a new one, but this branch is the one whose failure silently undoes the fix.)

samples.summary: Sibling image-API entry points still use the throwing doc.getBlock, so the remote-delete crash the new provider guards against remains reachable through them
samples.evidence: `imageSelectionProvider` was written with `doc.findBlock` because `getBlock` throws (`throw new Error(\`Block not found: ${blockId}\`)`, document.ts:187). But `getSelectedImage` (editor.ts:3654), `updateSelectedImage` (3667) and `selectImageAt` (3640) still call `doc.getBlock(...)` on the same `selectedImage.blockId` and additionally test `if (!block) return null;`, a dead check for a function that throws. Any host calling `getSelectedImage()` after a remote peer deletes the block gets an exception instead of null.
searchedFor: grep getSelectedImage across repo (no frontend callers found)

finding.evidence: The image hit branch of `handleImageMouseDown` (editor.ts:2502-2511) calls `e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation(); e.stopImmediatePropagation();` and sets `selectedImage`, but never calls `textEditor.focus()`. verdict.reason: The image-hit branch (editor.ts:2502-2511) really does select the image without ever focusing the hidden textarea, and it stops propagation in the capture phase (editor.ts:2522), so the only focus-on-click site (TextEditor.handleMouseDown, text-editor.ts:1673) never runs for an image click. Every piece of the new image clipboard plumbing is bound to that textarea (text-editor.ts:559-565; imageKeyHandler consulted at 854; handleCopy image branch 1190-1197; handleCut 1224-1231), and editor.ts registers no document/container keydown/copy/cut listener (only mousedown-capture, dragover, drop, contextmenu, scroll, transitionend, loadingdone). Nothing in the frontend restores editor focus on a canvas click: toolbar-focus-release.ts:117 releases focus to the body, and CommentComposer.tsx:140,189 takes focus with no handback. So when focus has left the editor (e.g. after using the comments composer), clicking an image shows selection handles but Cmd/Ctrl+C silently copies nothing - the exact defect the change exists to fix. Two of the reviewer's sub-claims are wrong and should be discounted, though neither supplies a counterexample: (1) in read-only, handleImageMouseDown returns at editor.ts:2454 BEFORE any stopPropagation, so the click does fall through and does focus the textarea via text-editor.ts:1673 - read-only simply has no image selection at all; (2) right-click is skipped at editor.ts:2456, so the context-menu Copy path (docs-context-menu.tsx:239 -> editor.ts:3337 focus + execCommand) does work. The keyboard path in edit mode with focus elsewhere remains broken with no guard anywhere.

mergedFrom.summary: `getSelectedImage` / `selectImageAt` / `updateSelectedImage` call the throwing `doc.getBlock`, so their `if (!block) return` guards are dead and a stale block id throws instead of returning null

finding.summary: `deleteSelectedImageInline` deletes 1 char at the stored image offset without re-validating the block/image, so a stale image selection either throws or deletes the wrong character
finding.evidence: editor.ts:2242-2252 does `const { blockId, offset } = selectedImage; docStore.snapshot(); doc.deleteText({ blockId, offset }, 1);` with no `doc.findBlock(blockId)` / `findImageAtOffset` check. Its sibling `imageSelectionProvider` (editor.ts:2256-2267) deliberately uses `findBlock` and re-checks `findImageAtOffset`, with a comment naming the exact hazard: "a block a remote peer just deleted". `MemDocStore.deleteText` -> `findBlockInAnyArray` throws `Block not found: <id>` (memory.ts:214-217, 331-353), so on that same remote-deletion scenario the Delete/Backspace route (`imageKeyHandler`, editor.ts:2309-2313) throws out of the keydown listener instead of returning null. If the block still exists but offsets shifted (remote insert before the image, or the text-selection cut path described in the next finding), the delete silently removes an unrelated character — data loss with an undo snapshot taken around it. This delta's new cut tests are the first coverage of the `imageDeleteHandler` wiring; the cut path happens to be guarded by the provider, the Delete path is not.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. editor.ts:2242-2252 `deleteSelectedImageInline` guards only `readOnly || !selectedImage`, then does `docStore.snapshot()` + `doc.deleteText({ blockId, offset }, 1)` with no `findBlock`/`findImageAtOffset` re-validation — matching the reviewer's quote verbatim. Its sibling `imageSelectionProvider` (editor.ts:2256-2267) does perform both checks and its comment names the exact hazard (a block a remote peer just deleted). The throw is real: document.ts:277-278 delegates to store.deleteText, and memory.ts:214-217 calls findBlockInAnyArray which throws `Block not found` at memory.ts:353. The Delete/Backspace route reaches it unguarded via imageKeyHandler (editor.ts:2309-2313), invoked from the raw keydown listener at text-editor.ts:854 (registered text-editor.ts:560) with no try/catch; notably TextEditor's own stale-block remote-deletion guard sits at text-editor.ts:858-864, i.e. AFTER the imageKeyHandler call, so it cannot protect this path. No other code invalidates the stale selection: I enumerated every `selectedImage` reference in editor.ts, and neither validateCursorPosition (editor.ts:979-987, whose docstring covers remote block deletion) nor restoreLocalCursor (editor.ts:3724-3738, described at 3727 as running on every remote change) clears it. Second mode also holds: if the block survives but offsets shifted, the unconditional 1-char delete removes an unrelated character under an undo snapshot — data loss. Crash plus data-loss on a collaboratively reachable path = critical, squarely in the correctness lane. No refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: When a text selection and a click-selected image coexist, the text branch of `handleCut` deletes the text but never clears the parent's image selection, leaving `selectedImage` pointing at a shifted offset
finding.evidence: The new test at copy-integrity.test.ts:285-303 institutionalises the state where `selectedImage` and a text range are live at once (`selectImageAt` then `_setSelectionForTest`, asserting `getSelectedImage()` is still non-null after the copy). The cut counterpart is unguarded: `handleCut` (text-editor.ts:1233-1253) takes the `hasSelection()` branch, calls `deleteSelection()`, and never touches `imageSelectionProvider`/`imageDeleteHandler`, so `selectedImage.offset` in editor.ts is left pointing into text that has moved. The render path (editor.ts:1853-1855) will then draw resize handles around whatever image now sits at that key, and a following Delete goes through the unvalidated `deleteSelectedImageInline` (editor.ts:2242). The same stale state is produced by the copy branch, but only cut mutates the document.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: handleCut's text branch (text-editor.ts:1233-1253) writes the clipboard, snapshots and calls deleteSelection() without ever invoking imageSelectionProvider/imageDeleteHandler (only the !hasSelection() branch at 1224-1231 does). The coexisting state is real, not a test artifact: copy-integrity.test.ts:364-384 deliberately establishes selectImageAt + a text range and asserts getSelectedImage() stays non-null, mirroring handleCopy's precedence (text-editor.ts:1188-1198). Nothing clears selectedImage on document mutation — all writes to it in editor.ts (2247, 2304, 2324, 2342, 2508, 2518, 3644, 3649, 3762) are image-key routing, image mousedown, the public API, or dispose. The stale offset is then consumed by the render path's raw map lookup (editor.ts:1853-1855) and, worse, by deleteSelectedImageInline (editor.ts:2242-2252), which does doc.deleteText({blockId, offset}, 1) with no findImageAtOffset validation (contrast getSelectedImage at 3652-3663, which validates) — so a following Delete removes an arbitrary character. A production path exists: handleImageMouseDown returns early without clearing selectedImage for BUTTON/INPUT/menu targets (editor.ts:2457-2464), clearSearchMatches installs a text range (editor.ts:3393-3402) and docs-find-bar.tsx:131-137 calls it then refocuses the editor, while imageKeyHandler passes Cmd/Ctrl+X through unchanged (editor.ts:2298-2300). The reviewer's test line cite (285-303) is off by one test, but the substance is accurate; no refutation ground applies.
